title: Sumayyah, the first martyr
hook: Sumayyah bint Khayyat, killed for her faith, is remembered as the first martyr of Islam
carry: the first to give her life

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bilal under the rock in the sun. Your line was: ahad. One. Did you say your one word of faith, out loud or under your breath? Day seven hundred thirty-seven.

A father, a mother, and their son. When Ibn Ishaq comes to the worst of the persecution in Mecca, he names this family together: Yasir, his wife, and their son Ammar. Men from the clan of Makhzum have taken them out into the heat of the city to make them give up the new faith. The mother has no powerful family to come and pull her away. Her name is Sumayyah bint Khayyat. The early biographers give her only a few lines, and tradition has kept those lines and retold them. Today: Sumayyah.
screen: `A FATHER, A MOTHER, A SON.` → `NO CLAN TO PULL HER AWAY.` → `SUMAYYAH BINT KHAYYAT.`

segments.voice: Start with who she was. The sirah books say she had been a servant in a household of Makhzum, married Yasir, a man from outside Mecca who lived there under that clan's protection, and had a son, Ammar. So when the family became Muslim, nobody stood between them and the clan. Bilal yesterday had no tribe behind him either. Ibn Ishaq says Quraysh turned hardest on the Muslims who had no clan to protect them. Ibn Majah reports from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that Sumayyah was among the first to make their Islam public, not just to hold it quietly. Then the end. Ibn Ishaq says the family was tortured in the heat of Mecca, and that Sumayyah was killed because she would accept nothing but Islam. Ibn Sa'd adds that Abu Jahl, one of the leaders of Quraysh, struck her with a spear, and he calls her the first martyr in Islam. That's where the title comes from. The Arabic word for martyr is shahid, and the same word is used in the Qur'an for a witness. A martyr, in that sense, is someone whose life becomes testimony. Notice how little the sources hand us. No speech. No last words. Just a choice, held under pressure, by someone the powerful thought did not matter. Tradition remembers her for it: in Ibn Sa'd's telling, the first life given in Islam was a woman's, and she was not one of the powerful.
screen: `A SERVANT, A WIFE, A MOTHER.` · `NO CLAN TO SHIELD HER.` · `SHE WOULD ACCEPT NOTHING BUT ISLAM.` · `SHAHID: A MARTYR, A WITNESS.`

segments.voice: The practice: remember someone who suffered for what they believed. Sit, and let your breathing settle. It can be someone from history, from any faith or none, or someone in your own family: a grandparent who kept their faith quietly in a hard place, a person who lost a job for refusing to lie. Hold their face, or their name, if you don't know the face. Say the name once, softly. You don't need to know how the story ended. Just keep them company for a minute, the way people have kept Sumayyah's name. If you pray, you can pray for them in your own words. The bell holds the time.
Sumayyah. Sumayyah bint Khayyat, mother of Ammar, killed in Mecca for her faith, whom Ibn Sa'd calls the first martyr in Islam. Today's word.
Your line: the first to give her life. Today, notice one person around you whom others overlook, and treat what they say as if it matters. Day seven hundred thirty-seven.

fork.setup: you're Sumayyah, out on the hot ground. the men want you to give up your faith. what do you do?
options: say what they want and go home.
refuse, and accept nothing but Islam.
fork.reveal: Ibn Ishaq says she would accept nothing but Islam, and was killed for it. Ibn Sa'd names Abu Jahl as the one who struck her.

original.note: Arabic: a martyr; the same word is used in the Qur'an for a witness.

trapdoor: what you thought: a name from a list of early Muslims.
what it means: a woman with no clan to protect her, killed for refusing to give up her faith.
what a scholar hears: Ibn Ishaq on the family of Yasir; Ibn Sa'd naming Abu Jahl and calling her the first martyr in Islam; shahid as witness.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Banu Makhzum torture Ammar, his father and mother; she is killed for refusing anything but Islam)
Ibn Sa'd, Kitab al-Tabaqat al-Kabir (Sumayyah bint Khayyat: struck by Abu Jahl; the first martyr in Islam)
Sunan Ibn Majah 150 (Ibn Mas'ud: those who first made their Islam public, including Sumayyah)

notes: 'The first martyr in Islam' is attributed to Ibn Sa'd's Tabaqat; confirm the wording and placement there (and in Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba if preferred).
Sumayyah's earlier status as a servant (mawla) of Abu Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira of Makhzum and Yasir's status as an ally (halif) of Makhzum are from Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Ishaq; confirm the framing.
Sunan Ibn Majah 150 number cited from memory; the hadith lists those who first declared their Islam (a count is given there, deliberately not repeated). Confirm.
'Shahid' as both martyr and witness: the script says the same word is used in the Qur'an for a witness (e.g. 2:282, shahidayn) rather than giving an etymology. Confirm.
The closing line 'the first life given in Islam was a woman's' leans on Ibn Sa'd's 'first martyr'; a Keeper may prefer to soften to 'tradition remembers'.
Ibn Ishaq's remark that Quraysh turned hardest on the Muslims with no clan protection is paraphrased; confirm.
